research_page.title: LEQEMBI (lecanemab) Prescribing Information (Jan 2026)
research_page.description: Official FDA prescribing information for lecanemab, including the 2026 addition of a subcutaneous autoinjector maintenance option.
research_page.takeaway_md: Lecanemab is an anti-amyloid monoclonal antibody approved for mild cognitive impairment or mild dementia stage Alzheimer's. It clears brain amyloid and slowed clinical decline by 27% on the CDR-SB over 18 months. The January 2026 label update adds a weekly subcutaneous maintenance autoinjector, though it retains strict boxed warnings for ARIA and requires ApoE4 testing.
key_findings_md: Slowed clinical decline by 27% (-0.45 points) on the CDR-SB over 18 months compared to placebo (Section 14, Table 10).
Reduced amyloid beta plaque to less than 30 Centiloids in 67% of patients by week 79 (Section 12.2).
ARIA occurred in 21% of treated patients, with ApoE4 homozygotes facing a 45% incidence rate compared to 19% in heterozygotes and 13% in noncarriers (Section 5.1).
research_page.methods_md: Information based on two double-blind, placebo-controlled trials: Study 1 (Phase 2, N=856) and Study 2 (Phase 3, N=1795). Patients had mild cognitive impairment or mild dementia with confirmed amyloid pathology.
research_page.trial_evidence_md: Lecanemab's efficacy is established by the pivotal Phase 3 Clarity AD trial ([NCT03887455](/trials/lecanemab-clarity-ad)) and the Phase 2b Study 201 ([NCT01767311](/research/papers/lecanemab-phase-2b)). Both trials demonstrated robust amyloid clearance and modest cognitive benefit. A minor discrepancy exists between the FDA label stating 1,795 randomized patients for Study 2 and the registry's 1,906 total enrollment, which simply reflects the modified intention-to-treat analysis population. The subcutaneous dosing option was evaluated separately in a Phase 1 bioequivalence study ([NCT05533801](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05533801)) and open-label cohorts, rather than in the core 18-month placebo-controlled trials.
research_page.sentiment_md: Public perception is divided. Patients and caregivers heavily favor the new subcutaneous IQLIK autoinjector for its convenience over bi-weekly IV infusions. However, clinicians continue to debate the clinical meaningfulness of a 0.45 CDR-SB benefit, and high-profile safety concerns regarding ARIA—particularly for APOE4 homozygotes—dominate scientific discussions. Misinformation also persists, with some public factions mistakenly believing the drug is a cure or that the subcutaneous option eliminates the need for intensive MRI monitoring.
caveats_md: While the subcutaneous autoinjector offers convenience, its clinical efficacy relies on pharmacokinetic modeling and open-label extensions rather than long-term, placebo-controlled data.
Although lecanemab clears amyloid in ApoE4 homozygotes, exploratory analyses showed no significant clinical benefit on the primary endpoint for this highest-risk subgroup.
Use of antithrombotic or thrombolytic medications increases the risk of severe intracerebral hemorrhage.
relates_to_md: [Lecanemab Phase 2b](/research/papers/lecanemab-phase-2b) — The proof-of-concept trial (Study 201) that informed the Phase 3 dosing strategy.
[Amyloid hypothesis](/research/amyloid-hypothesis) — The foundational theory that lecanemab targets by clearing amyloid plaques.

trial_pages.title: Clarity AD (Lecanemab Phase 3)
trial_pages.description: Pivotal Phase 3 trial evaluating lecanemab in early Alzheimer's disease with confirmed amyloid pathology.
trial_pages.population: Early Alzheimer's disease (MCI or mild dementia) with confirmed amyloid pathology
trial_pages.primary_endpoint: Change from baseline in CDR-SB at 18 months
trial_pages.why_md: Clarity AD serves as the pivotal confirmatory trial for lecanemab, testing whether clearing amyloid protofibrils translates to a measurable slowing of cognitive decline. It established the clinical dataset used for full FDA approval.
status_log_md: **2023-01-05** — Phase 3 primary results published in NEJM showing a 27% slowing of clinical decline.
trial_pages.results_md: Lecanemab met its primary endpoint, slowing cognitive and functional decline by 27% (-0.45 points on the CDR-SB) over 18 months. It significantly reduced amyloid burden, but increased the risk of Amyloid Related Imaging Abnormalities (ARIA), especially in APOE4 homozygotes.

timeline_entries.title: 2026-01 — FDA approves subcutaneous Leqembi autoinjector
timeline_entries.body_md: The FDA updated the [Leqembi prescribing information](/research/papers/leqembi-fda-label-2026) to include a weekly subcutaneous maintenance injection, offering a more convenient home-administered alternative to bi-weekly IV infusions.

notes_for_editor: The clinical-trials researcher accurately caught the 1,906 vs 1,795 enrollment discrepancy for Study 2. I have added a note in the trial_evidence_md section clarifying that 1,795 reflects the modified intention-to-treat population analyzed for efficacy.
